title: A Colony for the Vector
premise: Vesper Marchetti, a clone created to inherit the memories and unfinished work of the original Vesper, arrives at Meridian Deep to settle a murder case no one wants solved. The colony is dying quietly—air scrubbers failing, population dwindling, records sealed by the corporate charter that owns everything. When a distress signal in an extinct language surfaces from beneath the colony's foundations, Vesper discovers Meridian was built over the site of a massacre of the original settlers, erased from every archive. As corporate enforcers arrive to bury the evidence and the colonists themselves deny their own history, Vesper must choose between the loyalty they were cloned to owe the company and the truth the dead are demanding. In the end, Vesper broadcasts the massacre records on the extinct language's frequency—letting the dead testify—and burns their own inheritance, choosing justice outside the law at the cost of their identity.
about_author: Coral Galloway is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing defunct colonial charters before turning to fiction. She writes about places that outlive their paperwork, and people who outlive their names.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Dust
chapters.summary: Vesper Marchetti lands at Meridian Deep carrying the original's memories and a murder case file stamped dormant for eleven years. The colony is half-empty, corridors dark, air tasting of rust. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: dislocation—a person built from someone else's grief trying to feel it as their own.

chapters.title: The Client Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Vesper meets the charter administrator, Oduya, who insists the murder victim never existed in official records. The original Vesper's notes contradict this. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: first crack in the world's surface—the law here is whatever the charter says it is.

chapters.title: People Made of Weather
chapters.summary: Vesper interviews remaining colonists: a hydroponics priestess, a retired engineer drinking himself blind, children born underground who've never seen sky. They remember the victim fondly but refuse to speak on record. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: tenderness curdling into unease—the colony protects its silences like warmth.

chapters.title: Eleven Years Cold
chapters.summary: Working from the original's memory-fragments, Vesper reconstructs the crime scene in a decommissioned water reclamation bay. Evidence was scrubbed, but not perfectly. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: grim satisfaction turning to dread as the scrubbing proves institutional, not personal.

chapters.title: Signal Beneath the Floor
chapters.summary: During seismic surveying, Vesper's equipment catches a repeating transmission rising from under the colony—in a language extinct since the Diaspora Wars. The engineer recognizes a fragment his grandmother sang. POV: alternating Vesper and the engineer, Ilya. Emotional beat: awe and terror; the ground itself is speaking.

chapters.title: The Charter's Long Arm
chapters.summary: A corporate enforcement vessel announces unscheduled arrival. Oduya warns Vesper, privately, to conclude the case as accidental death. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: pressure closing in; loyalty to the original's mission now feels like a trap set by the company that made them both.

chapters.title: What the Dead Kept
chapters.summary: Following the signal, Vesper and Ilya breach a sealed sublevel: a settlement predating the charter, homes intact, and a mass grave of two hundred bodies the founding records say never lived. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: horror transfigured into purpose—the case was never one murder.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Names
chapters.summary: Among the remains, personal effects survive: a child's drawing, a ledger written in the extinct tongue. Vesper begins translating with the priestess's help. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: mourning without permission—grieving people history deleted.

chapters.title: Deny, Delay, Delete
chapters.summary: Enforcers land. Oduya publicly declares the sublevel structurally hazardous and orders it sealed. Colonists who helped Vesper start losing power rations. POV: Oduya. Emotional beat: corruption shown as banality—he believes he's protecting them from a truth that would kill the colony faster than failing air.

chapters.title: The Original's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Decoding a locked memory-block, Vesper finds the original had found the grave too—and chose to bury it, accepting the company's terms. The murder she investigated was punishment for someone else who talked. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: betrayal at the root of self; Vesper was cloned to repeat a cowardice.

chapters.title: Ilya's Grandmother's Song
chapters.summary: Ilya reveals the lullaby is a survivor's account: his ancestors hid in the tunnels while the first colonists were purged to make room for the charter. His family has sung the evidence for generations, unheard. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: inherited witness—memory as resistance when paper fails.

chapters.title: Sealed Doors, Open Wounds
chapters.summary: Enforcers weld the sublevel shut. A colonist who spoke to Vesper is deported on manufactured charges. The colony splits between fear and fury. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: guilt and resolve—the cost of asking questions lands on others first.

chapters.title: A Court With No Jurisdiction
chapters.summary: Vesper attempts legal channels: the charter's own arbitration clause. The hearing is a performance; the arbitrator is charter-employed. Justice exists on paper only. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: cold clarity—the law will not save anyone; it is the weapon being used.

chapters.title: The Priestess's Bargain
chapters.summary: The hydroponics priestess offers the colony's hidden archive—generations of off-record truth—if Vesper swears to protect the living before avenging the dead. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: moral weight shifting; truth-telling must serve survivors, not just the past.

chapters.title: Countdown in the Dark
chapters.summary: Vesper learns the enforcers' real mission: not sealing the grave but demolishing the entire sublevel—and the colony's life-support runs through it. The distress signal was a warning system still functioning after two centuries. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: ticking clock; forgetting isn't passive anymore, it's demolition.

chapters.title: Every Record Says Otherwise
chapters.summary: Vesper confronts Oduya with the original's confession. He breaks: he knew, always knew, and kept the colony alive by keeping it ignorant. He begs Vesper not to make the dying remember. POV: Oduya. Emotional beat: tragic symmetry—two custodians of a lie, one cowardly, one not yet decided.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Clone
chapters.summary: Vesper weighs the inheritance: the original's memories, loyalties, and shame are all they have of a self. Keeping them means silence. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: identity crisis at the threshold—whoever Vesper becomes, it won't be who they were made to be.

chapters.title: Broadcast on a Dead Frequency
chapters.summary: With the priestess, Ilya, and half the colony, Vesper hijacks the comm array and transmits the massacre record, the translation, and the original's confession—in the extinct language, letting the dead speak in their own voice, on open channels no corporation can unsend. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: catharsis; testimony as resurrection.

chapters.title: What the Enforcers Burn
chapters.summary: Enforcers move to destroy the array and the sublevel. Colonists stand in the tunnels, unarmed, singing the lullaby as cameras roll. The broadcast makes every act of erasure visible. POV: Ilya. Emotional beat: terror and defiance fused—power meets witnesses it cannot delete fast enough.

chapters.title: Judgment Outside the Law
chapters.summary: The charter, exposed, withdraws rather than face galactic scandal; the enforcers stand down mid-demolition. Oduya resigns and hands Vesper the true archives. No court convicts anyone—but the record now exists, and the colony holds its own reckoning. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: justice achieved imperfectly, outside every framework designed to prevent it.

chapters.title: Burial, Finally
chapters.summary: The colony buries the two hundred with names recovered from the ledger, read aloud in the extinct tongue. The original Vesper's ashes join them—her cowardice forgiven, her case closed at last. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: grief completed; the murdered and the murderer's legacy laid down together.

chapters.title: A Colony for the Living
chapters.summary: Months later, aid ships arrive answering the broadcast. Vesper, having burned the original's memory-blocks, stays as the colony's new archivist—recording what happens next instead of what was buried. The final entry is written in both languages. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: quiet rebirth—an identity chosen, a future recorded, a colony remembered back to life.
